clue.text: The charm of an academic's unpretentious home

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, an academic graduate, so the possessive gives MA'S
a cot is a small humble cottage, a modest dwelling

explanation.surface: A scholar's modest cottage has a certain charm about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky object or figure, a talisman kept to bring good fortune.

clue.text: The musician's fading away as the fellow is able to

parts.note: man means a fellow, a chap
can do means is capable of doing

explanation.surface: A performer fades as far as the man can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The musician's' signals a term from musical scores, which are mostly in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Mancando is an Italian score direction for the sound to die away gradually.

clue.text: Tops up credit arrangements — wide-ranging

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: caps are lids or tops
IOUs are notes promising repayment of a debt

explanation.surface: Someone boosts their credit facilities with broad generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means roomy or extensive, covering a large area.

clue.text: Solo management in the city

indicators.note: management means handling or arranging, so the letters of solo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-person business run in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Shrank from publicity about game

indicators.note: the publicity letters sit around the game, so about signals one piece wrapped round another

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone recoiled from the press coverage of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten a text, so the past tense means made smaller or cut down.

clue.text: A show with appealing characters?

parts.note: appealing usually means attractive, but here the characters make appeals, asking for alms

explanation.surface: A stage production with a charming cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1728 ballad opera by John Gay is set among thieves and paupers.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's ballad opera of 1728, set among London's thieves and paupers.

clue.text: This club could be the very thing for evening!

explanation.surface: A golf club recommended as perfect for a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with an angled metal head; also a pressing tool used to smooth creases out of clothes.

clue.text: Slightly damaged, but looked about right

indicators.note: the looked word goes round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: gazed means looked steadily

explanation.surface: Something was a little marked but appeared fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A grazed surface is scraped or lightly scratched, a superficial injury.

clue.text: To dock a dog is no great matter

explanation.surface: Cutting a puppy's tail is said to be trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking means removing the tail, so de-tailing a dog; a detail is also a minor point.

clue.text: Almost never start too soon

indicators.note: the start of the word never means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: early means before the proper time

explanation.surface: Advice that one should hardly ever begin ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean very close to but not quite, a straight synonym.

clue.text: No rating may be without instruction

indicators.note: the letters of no rating may be rearranged into something else, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A naval rating without a rank might lack training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a sailor, but the two words are just the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught or uneducated lacks knowledge for want of schooling.

clue.text: Talk of vain sort, once totally different

indicators.note: totally different tells us the letters of vain sort and once are wholly reordered

explanation.surface: Chatter from a conceited person who used to be quite unlike this.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an informal exchange of spoken words between people.

clue.text: A team's turning-point

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, written XI in Roman numerals, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A side reaches the decisive moment of its season.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which a body rotates, literally the point of turning.

clue.text: Many a viva is concerned with ethics

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword shorthand for many
a viva is an oral examination, so oral can stand for it

explanation.surface: A great many university oral exams deal with ethical questions.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is a spoken university exam, chiefly British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral describes matters of right and wrong conduct, the subject of ethics.

clue.text: A legendary animal — the old-fashioned back it

parts.note: ye is the archaic spelling of the in signs like ye olde shoppe

indicators.note: back tells us the word it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A mythical beast is told that old-fashioned ways support it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature of folklore, never proved to exist.

clue.text: A Greek imprisoned by a biblical pharaoh

indicators.note: the answer is shut up inside the words biblical pharaoh

explanation.surface: A Greek held captive by an Egyptian ruler from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Greek' means the Greek counterpart of the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to our A.

clue.text: Secret agent's investment?

explanation.surface: Where a spy puts his money.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is the fictional secret agent, so the possessive is Bond's; bonds are also fixed-interest securities bought as an investment.

clue.text: Complaint of those with second sight?

definitions.text: Complaint of those with second sight?

parts.words: Complaint of those with second sight?
parts.note: second sight suggests clairvoyance, but read literally it is seeing everything a second time, an eye disorder

explanation.surface: An ailment supposedly suffered by psychics.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplopia is a medical complaint in which a person sees two images of one object.

clue.text: He's agreed to allow dope to come in

parts.note: a dope is a fool, as is an ass
enter means come in

explanation.surface: A man has consented to let a drug be brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assents is a person who has given consent or approval.

clue.text: Ingrates, coming to grief, draw together

indicators.note: coming to grief means falling apart, so the letters of ingrates are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ungrateful people who suffer misfortune tighten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To astringe is to bind or contract tissues, the action of an astringent.

clue.text: They have to get to work on foot

definitions.text: They have to get to work on foot

parts.words: They have to get to work on foot
parts.note: seems to describe commuters walking to the office, but means people whose job is treating feet

explanation.surface: Commuters who must walk to their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Podiatrists are medical specialists who treat ailments of the feet.

clue.text: A large number inside will get a late meal

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
inner means inside

explanation.surface: A big crowd indoors will be served supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, typically taken in the evening.

clue.text: Having to do with class correction

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A matter concerning the improvement of a school group.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Reform means improvement by removing faults, putting something right.

clue.text: A particular time should be fixed

indicators.note: the letters of time are to be put right, set into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists on settling a specific hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular, used as a noun, is a single detail or point, as is an entry on a list.

clue.text: Hill-top pile-up

parts.note: sounds like a crash on a summit road, but means a heap of stones placed on a peak

explanation.surface: A traffic collision at the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of stones built as a marker or memorial, often on a summit.

clue.text: Having money, always look sly

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, from libra, so it can mean money
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A rich person forever wears a cunning expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to give a sidelong, knowing or lascivious glance.

clue.text: Seasonal decline

parts.note: a downturn tied to time of year, read also as the American name of a season and a drop

explanation.surface: A drop in trade at a particular time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for autumn also means a descent or decline.

clue.text: Name of hothead joining gang

indicators.note: joining means the head letter is attached after the gang, side by side

parts.note: a set is a group or gang of people
the head of the word hot is its first letter

explanation.surface: Identity of a quick-tempered man who has joined a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is a boy's name, the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.

clue.text: Romance to get excited at on-line

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of at on-line are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A love affair gets thrilling once it moves to the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a love affair, but here it is a language family descended from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Neo-Latin is the Latin of the Renaissance onwards, and Latin is the root of the Romance tongues.

clue.text: Modern, not retrogressive, as a man of science

parts.note: new means recent or modern

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the word not is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A forward-looking scientist who never looks back.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity.

clue.text: Small band surrounding a medico left incoherent

indicators.note: the small band encircles the other letters, so surrounding puts them inside

parts.note: a ring is a small circular band, as worn on a finger
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A little group gathers round a doctor who leaves without making sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling talk wanders aimlessly without logical connection, lacking clarity.

clue.text: Direct payment required

explanation.surface: Someone instructs that a fee be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone is to command or instruct them; a charge is also the price asked for something.
